 Hon'Ble Mr Justice Javed Iqbal Wani, Judge

1. In the instant appeal filed under and in terms of the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short the Act of 1988) Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company appellant herein, has questioned award dated 18th of August, 2022, (for short the impugned award) passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pulwama (for short the Tribunal) in a claim petition titled as "Feroz Ahmad Rather Vs.
Bilal Ahmad Bhat and Ors.",
2. Facts emerging from the record would reveal that the claimant respondent 1 herein filed the claim petition supra before the Tribunal on 21st of December, 2011, for the injuries claimed to have been suffered by him in road accident on 19th of June, 2011, while travelling in his own vehicle from Pampore to Srinagar, upon its collision with another vehicle (Maruti Car) bearing registration number JK01M-4822, being driven by respondent 3 herein.

The claimant respondent 1 herein,
besides impleading the above driver of the above said Maruti Car also impleaded the owner of the said vehicle (Maruti Car) as a party respondent in the claim petition, being respondent 2 herein,
besides impleading the present Insurance Company as respondent 3 in the claim petition and subsequently also impleaded National Insurance Company M.A. Road Srinagar as respondent 4 in the claim petition, owing to the fact that the aforesaid Maruti Car owned by respondent 2 herein was insured with the said National Insurance Company.

The Tribunal, after entertaining the claim petition issued notice to the respondent therein the claim petition and in response thereto respondents 1 and 2 herein appeared and filed objections thereto the claim petition, whereas the respondent 3 herein being the driver of the Maruti Car did not choose to appear and consequently came to be set ex-parte on 27th of December 2013.

Both the Insurance Companies i.e. National Insurance Company respondent 4 herein as well as Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company appellant herein filed objections to the claim petition and opposed the same.

4. The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings of the contesting parties, framed the following issues:-
1 "Whether on 19.06.20211 petitioner was travelling his vehicle bearing registration no. JK13B-5250 from Pampore to Srinagar and Maruti 800 bearing Registration no.
JK01M-4822 coming from the opposite direction driven by the Respondent no.1 rashly and negligently smashed against the Vehicle of the Petitioner resulting into huge damage to the Vehicle of the petitioner and the Petitioner severally injured and shifted to SMHS Srinagar where he was operated and his spleen was removed by an operation and the said accident has rendered the Petitioner Permanently Disabled?
OPP 2.
Whether the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the Respondent no. 1?
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to any compensation, if so, from whom and to what extent?
Whether the Petitioner is not entitled to any compensation under contributory Negligence?
OPR-3 5.

In order to prove the issues, onus whereof was put on the claimant respondent 1 herein, the claimant respondent 1 examined 4 witnesses besides appearing himself as his own witness, whereas the respondent 4 being appellant herein did not produce any evidence however, National Insurance Company respondent 4 herein produced one witness.

6. The Tribunal after adjudicating upon the claim petition in terms of the impugned award awarded an amount of Rs.12,65,000/- as compensation in favour of the claimant respondent 1 herein, while holding the appellant herein liable to pay an amount of Rs.10,65,000/-
and out of said amount of compensation and held respondent 4 herein liable to pay the rest of the amount of Rs.2,00,000/- with 6% interest as compensation to the claimant respondent 1 herein.

7. The appellant herein has assailed the impugned award in the instant appeal on the following grounds: -

sentences.text: 2 9 BECAUSE the Ld. Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact that it is an admitted case of the Respondent no.1 that the left arm of the Respondent no.1 was having trauma since childhood and the said injury/disability was not caused by the said accident and Hence the insurance Company cannot made liable to compensate on the pre-existing and underlying anomalies.
10. BECAUSE The Ld. Tribunal failed to appreciate the statement 1 made by in the Cross during child birth due to which he had lower power in his left arm as per discharge certificate available".

11. BECAUSE The Ld. Tribunal failed to appreciate that the damages under the head of "Future loss of income" would get attracted in those circumstances wherein the injuries arising out of the otherwise would have generally been able to perform, if the accident had not occurred.

That as far as the present case is concerned, the Injured even before the accident was suffering from a low power left arm from childhood and had accordingly identified for himself a suitable job of hence the aggravation, if any caused by the accident did not limit the Respondent no.1 to perform his job as he was doing earlier.
Hence the award under the head "Future loss of income" is perverse and non-application of mind and the award has been passed in a cursory manner.

12. BECAUSE The Ld. Tribunal failed to appreciate that the Respondent no.l was suffering from Left hand low Power and hence was not eligible to hold a driving license and was neither eligible to drive.

That this fact cannot be ignored that if the Respondent no.1 was medically fit to drive the vehicle and could exercise required control over the steering of the Vehicle to maneuver it correctly, the Accident could have been avoided.

13. BECAUSE The Ld. Tribunal failed to appreciate that a driving license obtained by not breach of Insurance Policy terms and conditions.
14. BECAUSE The Ld. Tribunal failed to appreciate that Ld. Magistrate in FIR no. 47 of 2011 was Respondent no.3 together.
15. BECAUSE the Ld. Tribunal failed to exercise the litmus test proposed by the Hon'ble Supreme compensating for permanent disability is it has to determine whether "such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity."
In the present circumstances the injured to perform the work as he was doing before the Accident.
16. BECAUSE The Learned Tribunal has failed to grant reasonable reduction on account of was physically eligible to do so.

17. 18. BECAUSE The Learned Tribunal has not granted any recovery rights in favor of the Appellant and against the Respondent No. 2 and 3.
19.
BECAUSE any deviation from the law or its principles renders the entire award void-ab-initio illegal being perverse.

20. BECAUSE the Learned Tribunal committed a grave error of Law by passing an award in ignorance of the law naid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
21. BECAUSE the impugned order suffers from complete non- application of mind and is therefore bad in law and is therefore liable to be set aside.
22. BECAUSE the impugned order runs contrary to the established principles of Law and is therefore liable to be set aside.
23. The Appellant craves leave to add any other ground at a later 1 stage with the permission of this Hon'ble Court.
24. That the Appellant has no other efficacious remedy left except to approach this Hon'ble Court.
25. That the Appellant has not filed any other Petition before this Hon'ble Court or the Hon'ble Supreme Court seeking similar relief.

26. That the pre-deposit in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) is being made by way of a demand draft drawn on Standard Chartered Bank in favour of the Registrar General, Delhi High Court, New Delhi.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. As has been noticed in the preceding paragraphs the Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings of the contesting parties, being the claimant respondent 1 herein and respondent 4 herein framed the aforesaid issues, while putting onus to prove issues 1, 2 and 3 upon the claimant respondent 1 herein, put the onus to prove the issue No. 4 upon the respondent 3 herein i.e. the appellant herein.

Further as has been noticed in the preceding paras the claimant, respondent 1 herein, produced the above witnesses in order to prove the aforesaid issues, whereas the respondent 3 appellant herein did not produce any witness or led any evidence in rebuttal thereto.

9. Perusal of the statement of witnesses produced by the claimant, respondent 1 herein would tend to show that the claimant respondent 1, has successfully discharged the onus put on him qua the issues onus whereof was put to him successfully and has been able to prove the said issues in general Bajaj Allianz General Insurance ... vs Feroz Ahmad Rather And Ors on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49132272/
4 and issue No. 1 in particular, to be precise, about the permanent disability suffered by him on account of the accident.

sentences.text: A deeper and closer examination of the statement of PW4, Dr. Tariq Ahmad Padroo would reveal that the said doctor has deposed that after clinical examination and thorough check-up of the patient (claimant respondent 4 herein) it came to be concluded that the patient was having disability of 50% at that point of time though owing its origin to a previous having got further deteriorated on account of the injury sustained by the claimant respondent 1 herein in vehicular accident in question.
It also gets revealed from the statement of the said doctor that the disability certificate pressed into service by the claimant respondent 1 herein before the Tribunal have had also been proved.

10. It also gets revealed from the statement of PW5 that the said witness has also endorsed the plea of claimant respondent 1 that he suffered injury to his spleen in the accident in question for which he was operated and though the said witness in his cross-examination had deposed that a patient without spleen can live normal life, yet did not rule out that complications can arise while also having deposed that the claimant respondent 1 herein have had a lower power in his left arm during his birth as per discharge certificate yet has not denied or disputed the fact in the said cross-examination that claimant respondent 1 herein did not suffer injuries in the vehicular accident to his said arm and consequently became permanently disabled.
11.

Having regard to the aforesaid position obtaining in the matter inasmuch as the facts of the case emerging from the record as also the judgments taken cognizance of by the Tribunal referred in the impugned Award it cannot but be said that the Tribunal has dealt with the matter rightly and appropriately without committing any irregularity or perversity therein and consequently passed a just and fair award impugned in the instant appeal.

Thus the aforesaid grounds urged by the appellant herein in the memo of appeal against the impugned award in view of the aforesaid analysis pale into insignificance, more so in view of the judgement of the Apex Court passed in case titled as "Anita Sharma and Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd and another" reported in 2021 (1) JKJ SC 140 wherein at para 22 following came to be observed:
"22.

entities.text: Anita Sharma and Ors. Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd and another" reported in 2021 (1) JKJ SC 140
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Equally, we are concerned over the failure of the High Court to be cognizant of the fact that strict principles of evidence and standards of proof like in a criminal trial are inapplicable in MACT claim cases.
The standard of proof in such like matters is one of the preponderance of probabilities, rather than beyond reasonable doubt.

One needs to be mindful that the approach and role of Courts while examining evidence in accident claim cases ought not to be to find fault with non-examination of some best eyewitnesses, as may happen in a criminal trial; but, instead should be only to analyze the material placed on record by the parties to ascertain whether the claimant's version is more likely than not true."
12.
Viewed thus for the aforesaid reasons the appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.
(JAVED IQBAL WANI) JUDGE SRINAGAR 08.11.2024
